neighbours.label: Continuity from the past into the present: something that has gone on for a long time and still does (continually operating, for decades, to this day)
fire: It is the oldest continuously running newspaper in the state.
Russia has supplied gas to the region for decades.
The custom survives to this day in several mountain towns.
This is the longest continually inhabited city in Europe.
The family has farmed this land for generations.
Their rivalry continues to this day in every derby.
The bakery has served the town for over a century.
It remains the oldest continually operating lighthouse on the coast.
quiet: It was a small newspaper in the state that closed in 1950.
Russia supplied gas to the region in 1970 and then stopped.
The custom died out in 1900 in several mountain towns.
This was a briefly inhabited camp in northern Europe.
The family farmed this land for one summer before selling it.
Their rivalry ended in 1998 after a famous derby.
The bakery served the town for one year before it closed.
It was a short-lived lighthouse on the coast, torn down in 1920.
